reduction.quote: **Theorem A (proved):** for all $n$, $a_{n+1}$ = successor of $a_n$ in $S_\infty=\bigcap_m S_m$; hence the sequence is EXACTLY $S_\infty\cap[a_1,\infty)$.
reduction.witness: Missing: an actual proof that an integer $m\ge a_1$ is a term iff $\gcd(m,a_i)>1$ for every $i$ (equivalently every term), i.e. that no term of the sequence is skipped and that $a_{n+1}$ is the successor of $a_n$ in $S_\infty$ rather than merely in $S_n$. The quoted line only asserts the statement with the parenthetical label '(proved)' and defers the argument ('Full proof (in progress — see approaches/ and lemmas/)'); no case analysis or derivation appears anywhere in the text.
reduction.load_bearing: The whole reduction of the sequence to a fixed set $S_\infty$ rests on this claim, and the text supplies only the assertion, not the argument.

lower_bound.quote: - Remaining crux: **prove shrinkage stops** (equivalently: finitely many permanents / $S_\infty$ finitely generated).
lower_bound.witness: Missing: a proof, valid for all terms, that membership depends only on primes in a fixed finite set — e.g. that any candidate divisible by a large prime is dominated by a smaller integer with the same small-prime support which is itself a term, hence $S_\infty$ has finitely many minimal elements. The quoted line explicitly labels this as the unproved remaining crux; the surrounding evidence is only empirical ('Empirics (100+ values of $a_1$ ...): shrinkage ALWAYS stops').
lower_bound.load_bearing: Without finiteness of the generating family, $L$ cannot be formed as a product of finitely many primes and no periodicity follows; the text itself identifies this as the missing step.

upper_bound.quote: So it suffices: $S_\infty$ is a union of residue classes mod $L$ (then $a_{n+T}=a_n+L$ for ALL $n$ with $T=\#(S_\infty\cap[1,L])$).
upper_bound.witness: Missing: a proof that for a concrete $L$ (product of the relevant primes) membership in $S_\infty$ is invariant under $m\mapsto m+L$ for every $m\ge a_1$, and that counting terms in a window of length $L$ yields $a_{n+T}=a_n+L$ from $n=1$. The quoted sentence only says such periodicity of $S_\infty$ 'suffices'; it is stated as a goal conditional on the unproved finiteness lemma, with no derivation of the residue-class structure or of the counting argument.
upper_bound.load_bearing: The final conclusion is obtained only by this assembly step, which the text states as a desideratum rather than proving.

Framework (transversals, S_infty) is sound in outline and the claimed structure (L product of primes, T = count in a window) is stated, but every mechanism is asserted '(proved)' with proofs deferred elsewhere; finiteness is explicitly the open crux, supported only by empirics.
